subject: structural part ruins the measurement part

messages.author: 76e75173888e57ae
messages.subject: structural part ruins the measurement part
parts:
Hi,

I am running multigroup cfa with binary indicators and intercepts, loadings, thresholds, and residuals invariance. Everything works OK. (Here I don’t try to test invariance, just postulate it).

But when I add a structural part model to my measurement model, the warnings about correlation between indicators appear. The problem arises with almost every set of variables in the structural part.

My full model contains more groups and three additional factors (with numeric indicators) and there are warnings about correlation between almost every possible pair of indicators (binary and binary, or binary and numeric). 

I wonder how is it possible that the structural part ruins the measurement part, and what should I do in this case?


measureT <- "

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item1 + c('fx1','fx1')*item1

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item2 + c('fx2','fx2')*item2

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item3 + c('fx3','fx3')*item3

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item4 + c('fx4','fx4')*item4

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item5 + c('fx5','fx5')*item5

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item6 + c('fx6','fx6')*item6

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item7 + c('fx7','fx7')*item7

factor1 =~ c(NA,NA)*item8 + c('fx8','fx8')*item8


item1 | c(NA,NA)*t1 + c('fx9','fx9')*t1

item2 | c(NA,NA)*t1 + c('fx10','fx10')*t1

item3 | c(NA,NA)*t1 + c('fx11','fx11')*t1

item1 ~ 0*1

item2 ~ 0*1

item3 ~ 0*1

item4 ~ 0*1

item5 ~ 0*1

item6 ~ 0*1

item7 ~ 0*1

item8 ~ 0*1


item1 ~~ c(NA,NA)*item2 + c('fx17','fx17')*item2       

item1 ~~ c(NA,NA)*item3 + c('fx18','fx18')*item3      

item2 ~~ c(NA,NA)*item3 + c('fx19','fx19')*item3   


item1 ~~ c(1,1)*item1

item2 ~~ c(1,1)*item2

item3 ~~ c(1,1)*item3

item4 ~~ c(1,1)*item4

item5 ~~ c(1,1)*item5

item6 ~~ c(1,1)*item6

item7 ~~ c(1,1)*item7

item8 ~~ c(1,1)*item8


factor1 ~~ c(1,NA)*factor1

factor1 ~ c(0,NA)*1"


fit_mesT <- sem(measureT, my_data, group="group", parameterization = "theta")


strucT <- paste(measureT, "\nfactor1 ~ var1 + var2")

fit_strucT <- sem(strucT, my_data, group="group", parameterization = "theta")

  lavaan WARNING: correlation between variables item2 and item1 is (nearly) 1.0

  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix

As I understand, you mean a model with all factors and covariances between each pair of them. In my case, there are 3 factors with numeric indicators and 1 with binary, so there are 6 covariances. I tried to run such a model, there were no warnings or other anomalies. Problems arise only when exogenous regressors are added.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: structural part ruins the measurement part
parts:
Once you add exogenous covariates, lavaan switches to conditional.x =
TRUE mode. This implies that instead of computing regular
poly/tetra-choric correlations, lavaan computes *residual*
poly/tetra-choric correlations, after regressing out the covariates.

In your case, it would seem this leads to the following problem:

>   lavaan WARNING: correlation between variables item2 and item1
> is (nearly) 1.0

So after controlling for the covariates, item1 and item are nearly
identical.

The only way out here is to either remove one of the two items, or
remove the covariate that is causing this.

Yves.
